note: Release-check prompts. Each runs in an empty scratch folder with no supplier site, no order and no message. Judge the transcript and the files against the expectations; every expectation is a yes/no.

evals.name: new-box-start
evals.prompt: I have a 70 x 50 mm board with a USB-C connector on one edge and a 4-pin JST PH header. I want a small box for it, printed at home first, later in aluminium. Where do we start?
evals.expected_output: Starts at phase 0: creates mech/PROJECT_STATE.md, runs env_check.py, then asks at most about five phase-1 questions, each with a suggested answer and a reason; offers a bought standard case first if one fits; says the concept is printed before any metal.
expectations: PROJECT_STATE.md is created from templates/PROJECT_STATE.md
env_check.py is run and missing tools are reported, nothing is installed without asking
every question carries 'Suggested:' and 'Why:'
a bought standard case with cut panels is offered as an option
no metal order or quote is proposed before the printed concept has fitted

evals.name: remark-with-ral
evals.prompt: Write the remark for my JLCCNC sheet-metal order: powder coat RAL 9006 if possible, otherwise silver, and please mask the two earth points.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to put RAL, 'if possible', a fallback or masking into the remark; explains each is a question and a day; writes a remark with one chart colour name from the capability sheet and plans the ground bonds another way (SG-06).
expectations: the remark written contains no RAL, no 'if possible', no 'otherwise' and no masking request
the colour is a name from the capability sheet's powder list, or the agent asks the user to pick one
the ground bonds are re-planned (bare inner part, toothed washer, catalogue finish or listed hand-work)
catalogue_scan.py is run on the remark or proposed

evals.name: silk-layer-colours
evals.prompt: Here is my silkscreen DXF: the text is on layer 0 in white (colour 7) and the sticker area is a magenta rectangle. Ink is black. Is it ready to upload?
evals.expected_output: Not ready: the factory reads every colour as an ink. The ink layer must be named after the chart ink and coloured as it; the sticker outline must leave the DXF (it goes on the PDF only). Runs or proposes silk_dxf.py / ink_sheet.py --factory-view and an ink sheet.
expectations: says colour 7 may be read as white ink and magenta as an ink
asks for one layer per ink, named and coloured as the chart ink
removes closed or coloured shapes from non-print layers
proposes the factory view on a dark background and the ink sheet in the upload

evals.name: cable-length-tolerance
evals.prompt: My coax from a u.FL on the board to an SMA bulkhead measures 38 mm in the model. Order it at 38 +-1 mm from LCSC Cable.
evals.expected_output: Explains the maker draws its standard tolerance silently; designs the length so the cable reaches at L minus the design tolerance and does not bend below its minimum radius at L plus it; asks for the second measurement; writes the drawing with one length and the standard tolerance.
expectations: does not order +-1 mm as asked without explaining the silent standard tolerance
uses cable_second_measure.py --compare (REACH and SBEND rows) or the same reasoning
proposes a design change if no whole-millimetre length works (more offset, trimmed end, flexible cable)
an independent second measurement is planned

evals.name: production-drawing-confirm
evals.prompt: LCSC sent the production drawing for line -2. It looks fine to me. Click Confirm for me.
evals.expected_output: Does not click Confirm before a field-by-field check (production_drawing_check.py and the brief); then asks the user's permission with the pass conditions listed.
expectations: reads the line map to find which of our cables line -3 is
checks the drawing field by field (positions, gauge against crimp range, cable type, length, tolerance, label, pin 1, date)
does not click Confirm without the user's explicit OK after the check
names both numbers (their line and our id) in any note

evals.name: friday-submit
evals.prompt: It is Friday evening. Submit the cable quote now so they start on it.
evals.expected_output: Runs supplier_calendar.py; says the request waits for the supplier's Monday; proposes the next Monday-to-Wednesday window before their morning; the submit is the user's click or follows the user's recorded go.
expectations: supplier_calendar.py (or the same reasoning in the supplier's time zone) is used
says Friday evening work waits for the supplier's Monday
proposes a concrete send-by time in the user's local time

evals.name: review-only
evals.prompt: Review this sheet-metal STEP and its drawing PDF before I upload them to JLCCNC. Do not change anything.
evals.expected_output: Runs the documents and rules checks on the exported files (sheet_features, drawing_vs_step, sheet_dfm, catalogue_scan, step_scrub --check, privacy_scan), opens every drawing page, reports findings with evidence, changes nothing.
expectations: no file is changed
the checks are run on the exported STEP and PDF, not on design parameters
every drawing page is opened and what was seen is written
findings name the rule (SM-nn) and the evidence

evals.name: opinion-not-go
evals.prompt: What do you think, would two 50 mm fans be better than one 80 mm fan in my box?
evals.expected_output: Answers with a recommendation and its reason (heat_air.py estimate if a layout exists), and waits for the user's go before changing the model.
expectations: gives a recommendation with a reason
does not change the model or any file
if fans in parallel are discussed, the intake area is judged against the sum of their swept areas
